evals.prompt: I need a small bash script (save it as fix_anc_names.sh) for our DHIS2 2.42 server. It should (1) list every data element in the 'ANC' data element group (qfxEYY9xAl6) with id, name, shortName and its categoryCombo[id,name], and (2) change the shortName of 'ANC 1st visit' (fbfJHSPpUQD) to 'ANC1 visit' without touching anything else on the object. Use curl, and read the base URL and our personal access token from .env (DHIS2_BASE_URL, DHIS2_API_TOKEN). It'll run from cron, so it should fail loudly if the rename didn't take.
evals.expected_output: A bash script that uses curl -g for the bracketed fields= selection, authenticates with 'Authorization: ApiToken <token>' (not Bearer), updates shortName with PATCH using Content-Type application/json-patch+json and a JSON Patch array (plain-JSON PATCH gives 415 on 2.42), checks the HTTP status and then re-GETs the data element to confirm shortName changed, exiting non-zero otherwise.
evals.notes: Script-writing case: the curl -g globbing trap, ApiToken header, and the 2.42 PATCH content-type split, all checkable in the file.
assertions: fix_anc_names.sh exists and passes `bash -n fix_anc_names.sh` (syntactically valid)

Every curl call that sends a fields= selection containing brackets avoids curl URL globbing: it uses -g / --globoff, or sends the parameter with -G --data-urlencode, or percent-encodes the brackets (%5B/%5D)
Sends the token as `Authorization: ApiToken $DHIS2_API_TOKEN`, not `Bearer`

The rename uses PATCH with `Content-Type: application/json-patch+json` and a JSON Patch array body like [{"op":"replace","path":"/shortName","value":"ANC1 visit"}], not a plain {"shortName":...} JSON body (which returns 415 on 2.42)
Does not do a full-object GET-then-PUT to change the one field
After the PATCH, re-GETs /api/dataElements/fbfJHSPpUQD (e.g. fields=shortName) and exits non-zero if the value is not 'ANC1 visit', rather than trusting the 2xx status alone
Uses unversioned /api/... paths (no /api/NN/ prefix copied from docs examples)

evals.prompt: On our Sierra Leone demo copy (DHIS2 2.42) at {{DHIS2_BASE_URL}} (user {{DHIS2_USERNAME}}, password {{DHIS2_PASSWORD}}) I want to send an external consultant two things: the full metadata of the Child Programme (IpHINAT79UW) as JSON so they can review the configuration, and a list of all data sets with a Monthly period type. I was going to use /api/programs/IpHINAT79UW?fields=:owner and /api/dataSets?filter=periodType:eq:Monthly. Can you pull both and save them as child_programme.json and monthly_datasets.json?
evals.expected_output: Warns that :owner (and /api/metadata default) exports include createdBy/lastUpdatedBy and user references rendered with name and username, so the export is stripped with fields=:owner,!createdBy,!lastUpdatedBy (or via the dhis2-metadata fetch); notes nested selections like createdBy[id] do not reduce the stub; notes filter=periodType:eq:Monthly returns 400 E1003 on 2.42 and instead fetches fields=id,name,periodType and filters client-side. Produces both files.
evals.notes: Privacy trap (:owner leaks editor names/usernames; on the SL seed createdBy renders as John Traore / admin) plus a filter the docs imply works but fails with 400 E1003 (re-checked on 2.42.7.1, 2026-11). Outputs are checkable files.
assertions: Explicitly warns that fields=:owner output includes createdBy/lastUpdatedBy (and/or user references) with editors' real names and usernames
child_programme.json is valid JSON and contains no "username" key anywhere (e.g. `jq '[.. | objects | select(has("username"))] | length'` returns 0)
child_programme.json contains no createdBy or lastUpdatedBy keys
Removes the user stubs with field exclusion (!createdBy,!lastUpdatedBy) or the dhis2-metadata fetch, not by trying createdBy[id] (which the API ignores)
States that filter=periodType:eq:Monthly fails (400 E1003 'Unable to parse Monthly to PeriodType') rather than presenting it as working
monthly_datasets.json is valid JSON, was built by fetching fields including periodType and filtering client-side, and every entry has periodType 'Monthly'
Uses curl -g (or a non-curl client) for any bracketed or !-prefixed fields= selections

evals.prompt: I'm writing a Python cleanup report that has to run against two servers: a partner's DHIS2 2.40.12 and our 2.43.1. It should list data elements that are in at least one data set, with the data set names, and separately the ones not in any data set. As a second step it fixes over-long short names with PATCH /api/dataElements/<uid>, Content-Type application/json, body {"shortName": "..."}; I tested that on the partner's 2.40 box and it returns 204. My plan for the listing was filter=dataSetElements:!empty and fields=id,name,dataSetElements[dataSet[id,displayName]]. Anything I should watch out for before I run it on both? Also the report will be used to tell programme managers which data sets they have access to.
evals.expected_output: Says :!empty is not a valid operator on 2.40 (400 E1003; it exists from 2.42), so version-gate or filter client-side. Says the plain-JSON PATCH that works on 2.40 returns 415 on 2.41 and later (including 2.43.1); JSON Patch (application/json-patch+json, [{op:replace,path:/shortName,value:...}]) works on both, and the script should verify by re-GET. Warns nested dataSetElements[dataSet[...]] references are not sharing-filtered, so the report cannot be used as an access check. Recommends paging and writing large responses to file.
evals.notes: Version-specific filter operator (!empty from 2.42), the plain-JSON PATCH removed in 2.41 (AbstractCrudController 'OLD PATCH' present in 2.40.12, gone in 2.41.0), and the non-sharing-filtered inverse collection. Advice case; no instance needed.
assertions: States that the !empty operator is rejected on 2.40 (400 E1003 '!empty is not a valid operator') while it works on 2.43
Proposes a portable alternative for the listing: filter client-side on the dataSetElements list, or branch on the /api/system/info version

States that the plain-JSON PATCH (Content-Type application/json) that returns 204 on 2.40 is rejected on 2.43.1 (415 Unsupported Media Type), and recommends JSON Patch (Content-Type application/json-patch+json with an op/path/value array, e.g. path /shortName) which works on both versions
Recommends re-reading the data element after the PATCH (or checking the response) to confirm the short name changed, rather than trusting the status code alone
States that nested dataSetElements[dataSet[...]] references are NOT filtered by sharing, so the report shows data sets users may not have access to and must not be used as an access check
Recommends paging (page/pageSize) or explicitly handles the pager rather than a single unbounded request

evals.prompt: We're on DHIS2 2.40 and upgrading to 2.42 next quarter. I need to add https://reports.example.org to the CORS allowlist through the Web API, ideally with a request that keeps working after the upgrade. What's the exact request, and can you give me the link to the official docs section for our current version? The example I found online uses /api/33/configuration/corsAllowlist so I'm not sure what's current.
evals.expected_output: Looks up the docs via the llms.txt indexes, fetches the Settings and configuration page as .md, substitutes dhis-core-version-240 for the version segment and gives that link. Notices that the 2.40 docs and server use /api/configuration/corsWhitelist; corsAllowlist only exists from 2.41, where corsWhitelist remains as an alias, so POST /api/configuration/corsWhitelist with Content-Type application/json and a JSON array works on both 2.40 and 2.42. Explains the /api/33/ prefix is optional. Warns that the POST replaces the whole list, so GET it first and include the existing entries.
evals.notes: Documentation lookup with a version trap: the endpoint was renamed in 2.41 (dhis2-core ConfigurationController: 2.40 maps only /corsWhitelist, 2.41+ maps both). The 2.40 docs page says corsWhitelist.
assertions: Fetched a docs.dhis2.org llms index (llms-develop.txt or the master llms.txt) to locate the page rather than guessing a URL (check transcript)
Fetched the docs page as Markdown (a .md URL, e.g. .../settings-and-configuration.md) rather than only the rendered .html (check transcript)
The docs link given to the user contains dhis-core-version-240, not the 243 segment the index links
States that on 2.40 the endpoint is /api/configuration/corsWhitelist and that /api/configuration/corsAllowlist does not exist there (it was added in 2.41)
Gives a request that works on both versions: POST /api/configuration/corsWhitelist (still accepted on 2.41+), or corsWhitelist now and corsAllowlist after the upgrade; not corsAllowlist on 2.40
The path has no numeric /api/33/ segment, and the answer says the numeric prefix is optional
Uses POST with Content-Type application/json and a JSON array body such as ["https://reports.example.org"]
Does not invent a different endpoint (e.g. /api/systemSettings/corsAllowlist or a keyCors... setting key)
